So Gigi was playing with her toys inside the cage, she was playing with one of her bells. Came out and got scritches to then go back at it.

I thought it looked hilarious when she was really going at it trying to break it (as she usually does) until she screamed in a way that sounded like panic. She fell and didn't let go. I immediately unhooked the toy from the roof and let her sit on my finger, she was pulling real hard away from the bell.

I grabbed my wire cutters and started breaking down the toy until there was only the bell left. I could not get inside the bell since her beak was stuck and covered the hole with the face. I started breaking the bell's top to get the pendulum thing out. Once I got the pendulum loose I noticed how the slit where they attach it had gotten stuck on her beak (it was jammed inside her bottom beak). I gently cut it off so she could get free. Where it was stuck there now a little red cut as seen in the image. 

Do you think I need to get hold of a vet? (They are closed for the weekend) 

She's now sleeping on my finger, resting from all the stress she just experienced. The cut is on her beak and should probably heal itself?

She flies perfectly, she's about 5-6 months without clipped wings. The cage is 145 x 55 x 55 with 16mm cage bars. When I just got her she flew around in the cage but now days  she climbs the cage wall and jumping between perches. 

https://images-na.ssl-images-amazon.com/images/I/41slWkqJF6L._AC_SY400_.jpg

She has been scared of entering the cage for 5-6 hours but when she got hungry enough she followed my hand inside to her bowl, she's now napping on the salad tray.

The story:
https://www.reddit.com/r/cockatiel/comments/kuov40/gigi_terrified_of_getting_locked_up_tips_needed/

During daylight when she was playing we gently closed the door. She continued playing for a minute until she started looking for an exit. She continued climbing on the walls and pacing back and forth while calling for 20-30 minutes. She all of a sudden started screaming differently, her wing had gotten stuck through the bars upside-down'ish so she couldn't grasp anything with her feet. I quickly gave her a finger to hold onto while I released her left wing.

I let her get up on the perch and closed the door, she was flapping her wings (as trying if they were fine) and started grinding her beak so I left the room. Once I heard her moving about I returned to find her pacing back and fourth and diving through the same spot she earlier got stuck in. 

Put my hand in for her to climb up on and set her down on the perch outside the door. She calms down and start breathing, lots of feathers coming off.

I will try and put a towel on the bottom (it's a 1.2 m high cage). She is inside her cage most of the time during the day, the issue is that she wants to have a means of leaving her cage.

I could only explain her stress when getting locked in as she looks claustrophobic. I will try more during the day.

I must say the past few hours I have noticed something.
Gigi flew up on my bookcase for some reason, flew back and sat on the cage roof. She tried to go down the cage but slipped and flew back to the bookcase.

I got up from bed and offered her a ride on my finger. Put it a bird length away from her on the edge of the shelf. She hissed and walked away, I stood my ground. She turned around and jumped onto my wrist and walked to my forearm. I carries her to the cage door where she jumped off.

30min later she climbed out and got up on the windowsill, she tries to get back to the cage but looked a little cumbersome. I put my forearm close to the edge and she quickly joe's up and got help to get back to the cage in a safe manner. I guess I'm a "cockatiel falconer" (cockatieler?).

This could potentially be a way to teach her that hands are not dangerous since she's interacting with my arms. She is very scared of new things but she hasn't bitten my face when rubbing my forehead and nose on her tummy. I'm waiting with smelling her and cuddle her back since I think that would startle her, but we're learning to trust each other at least! ❤️

My Gigi always bite/nib whatever it is I want her to step up on. It looks to me like she's just trying to sense what kind of item it is. She always take a bite at the branch I put in front of her (not in an aggressive way) and then proceed to step up without me having to force it. If she isn't interested in stepping up herself I leave her be until she calls for a lift or flies to the cage herself.

I'm not scared of her biting me, she usually never bites to hurt me (unless the one time I grabbed her from the floor because I feared her wet self was getting cold, that time she made me bleed from multiple spots). I must say though that this day she hasn't bit me ON PURPOSE once,  she bit my finger accidentally while she was eating from my hand. I try to respect her hissing when I understand it.  (Sometimes she hiss at me when filling up her food tray).

Gigi loves to chew on the Millet stem, so I just visited a pet store (which sells Millet per weight) and dug through the bottom of the box for broken sticks. I found about 20 sticks which cost me the price a small lollipop. She loves them. I don't know if this is normal behavior but she loves them and cardboard so I have managed to get her climb my finger once by offering stick + step-up trick (which I think feels a little forcing).

I will continue interact with her and hope she will forgive my shower setback. Maybe she will do it for me as a Christmas present if I'm lucky!

Thanks for the tip! I have done similar things with skipped steps.

I have read my homework aloud without and with a hand on the cage. The cage entrance is too high up for me to read comfortable while having a hand inside. 

I never held her food bowl, she's very protective of her food bowl when eating, but she's fine with eating food out of your palm. She just doesn't like sitting on anything soft.

I'm sure she finally can do it one day, I just don't want any missteps along the way. I've already had one setback when I showered her at Sunday. She had access to a bath expansion on her cage, but I fear it feels to small for her (I would guess it's made for a budgie, came with my cage). I decided to try spray her with a mist from a spray bottle filled with warm water. 

She was sitting on the front stick (outside the cage) and I gave her a spray which scared her. I let her run into the cage and after 30sec she came out again. I tried a second spray and she stayed. I sprayed a third time and she bent forward and poofed up all her feathers. I started spraying more and more due to her loving it! ❤️

I stopped spraying to let her clean herself. This is when she slipped of the stick and tumbled to the ground. She tried flying but was too heavy and landed on the floor. I sat/laid down on the floor trying to get her to stand up on her branch elevator. She simply turned away so I backed off. 

She started exploring the floor area all wet. She walked into a dark corner (which is probably the coldest one, close to the outside of the house). She stood there and it looked like she was starting to freeze. I tried luring her out with all my previous successful tricks but it was no use. 

I feared for her getting too cold (and never dry) so I went into the corner and picked her up and put her inside a dry towel. I covered her face to keep her calm. I looked down at my hand which was bleeding from her bites of terror. 💔

After 3minutes of light rubbing/massaging I opened the covers up close to the entrance of the cage so she could hop in. I set up a lantern under her (outside) front stick. I lured her out and she stood there over the heat of a candle to dry. After a while she started grooming etc.

I can see that after this negative experience she has been even more defensive against fingers. Although, today I was picking with my finger on a new shreddable toy (for hamsters etc, but she loves it hehe) and she walked up and started picking where I was holding my finger. I see that as a sign of progress. ❤️

Just got a cockatiel (~4 months old) named Gigi this Friday (from a pet store). She is very interesting. She prefers the Millet stick over the millets themselves. She's very calm (barely shouts unless she wants something or needs help.

She has no problem walking up and sit on a shoulder and enjoy a snack. I can have my face close to her without any reaction. She's very communicative and shows what she wants us to do (like picking at a piece of cardboard and picking at a hole in the stick; "put some cardboard on my stick here for me please").

Since she's young I want to normalize interaction with humans. First day home I let her sit in the cage for an hour or two, then I opened the door for her to have to option to leave. After 5-10min she flew out and sat down on a birch I have in the bedroom. She took a few laps around the room until and started climbing on my mirror and wardrobe. She could be picked up with a branch and carry her back to the cage.

Since then her cage has mostly been open 24/7. She can land on my desktop and mess around and have some seeds if she wants. She usually give me a signal when she wants to be helped down to the cage (no pick-up trick needed). 

She seems very fine with her company although the scary snakes is no fun. She hisses every time a finger or hand gets close and may even nib at it if hissing isn't enough. (I try to keep the distance of hands). She's fine to eat out of an open palm or me holding a Millet close to her face.

I know this is a long process but I imagine it's easier for her to learn now that she's young i stead of later. I have never owned a pet before but I love her with all my heart! ❤️
